status: Water quality/performance follow-up; a local implementation milestone, not a photorealistic production-readiness or CryEngine-parity claim.
changes: Per-body wet-ground strength and vertical wet-bank extent; darkening and lower roughness extend from connected water without wetting isolated dry depressions.
Procedural shallow caustics affect directly lit terrain only, fade with depth/visibility, and freeze at zero animation speed. This is an approximation, not physically traced focusing.
Water caps temporal-history contribution through the existing HDR alpha channel, without another render pass. Opaque foliage retains its normal stabilization.
Scenery reflection traces use a shorter bounded march and cheaper depth reconstruction, and defer weak reflection angles to the existing environment reflection.
New shoreline textures stage before authoring commit; allocation failures retain the document/selection/history and can be retried.
Windows test/benchmark Chrome now selects the RTX 5060 using a freshly enumerated DXGI adapter LUID. It changes no user/browser/OS graphics preferences.

validation.build: npm run build passed on the final source, including strict type checks, runtime declarations and editor production output.
validation.lint: npm run lint passed; changed-file Prettier checks passed.
validation.unit: npm test -- --testTimeout=15000: 37 files, 284 tests passed. Uses the existing documented extended timeout for large fixtures.
validation.browser: 12 distinct Chrome scenarios passed across material-authoring (2), temporal-aa (1), water authoring/recovery (2), water lighting (1), and navigation (6). The new fixture initially used an unsupported tone-mapping value and the wrong runtime update argument; both fixture errors were corrected before its passing runs. Full browser suite not rerun.
validation.recovery: Injected both R32F bathymetry and RGBA32F shoreline allocation failures, retained document/redo/body selection, and verified successful retries.
validation.visual: Inspected the built runtime shallow-water fixture and the dense tropical coastal screenshots. The water fixture verifies dry-bank preservation, direct-only animated caustics and exact legacy shading restoration. The tropical comparison is dominated by the finite terrain's boundary wall, so it is a performance stress view rather than a finished photorealistic beach composition.

method.command: npm run dev -- --port 5190 --strictPort; node scripts/benchmark-water.mjs <external scene.terrain> <report.json> http://127.0.0.1:5190 [coast|canopy]
method.source: Unchanged external Tropical Grove — banana trail; 88 m terrain, 7,323 plants. Water is added in benchmark memory, never saved into the content project.
method.device: NVIDIA RTX 5060 Laptop GPU, Chrome 155, Windows ANGLE D3D11, 1920 x 1080 fullscreen first person, one unfinished GPU frame.
method.sampling: 2.5-second warmup then 180 rendered frames for water off, sky reflections and scenery reflections. Reported GPU timer covers environment rendering; CPU timing covers JavaScript render submission. FPS is wall-time submission cadence, not display scanout.
method.comparison: Before/after use identical project bytes and camera. The final preset additionally enables wet banks and caustics. A trial terrain projection optimization was removed before final measurements because its benefit was not established.
limits: Short static views, local background/clock/thermal variability and sequential mode order; do not infer a precise percentage speedup from these runs.
The canopy has little visible water. Coast and canopy observations do not establish sustained 30 FPS throughout the scene.
No physical mouse-to-display measurement, cross-device audit or long-session memory/performance soak.

remaining: Off-screen/planar reflections, spectral waves and breaking surf/crest whitecaps.
Physically focused caustics, volumetric scattering and dedicated water motion vectors.
Drying history, prop wetness/caustics, worker-based basin/shore preparation and finer outline editing.
A finished coastal content composition with authored seabed beyond the finite heightfield.
